description.value: Halverson House is a historic building within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, a National Historic Site in the Cariboo region of British Columbia. Barkerville preserves over 125 heritage buildings from the Gold Rush era along Williams Creek, with costumed interpreters, working displays, and museums bringing 19th-century life to vivid detail. Touring cyclists on the Gold Rush Trail will find the site a compelling stopover, though it is remote and set deep in the forests and mountains of the Cariboo.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies Halverson House as a history museum building within Barkerville. The website at barkerville.ca describes the entire Barkerville Historic Town & Park — a National Historic Site with 125+ heritage buildings, accommodations, campgrounds, and seasonal programming through 2026. Halverson House is not specifically mentioned on the fetched pages, and no cycling-specific amenities (bike parking, water refill, washrooms) are confirmed for the individual building or the wider site. The website confirms the site is actively operating with 2026 seasons planned. OSM has no address or phone; the website does not provide a street address or phone on the fetched pages.
